summary: The Bipartisan Policy Center supports preserving E-Rate as a core part of the Universal Service Fund and an ongoing national responsibility, not a one-time deployment. The program has demonstrated significant progress in providing connectivity to schools, and its progress is evidence of its effectiveness, not a reason for sunset or limitation. The text discusses the impact of ending the E-Rate program on school districts, the importance of connectivity in schools beyond student screen time, and the need for the program to cover all types of communities, not just rural areas. It also highlights the cost savings and the need to evaluate E-Rate funding based on educational outcomes rather than screen time limits. BPC urges the Commission to preserve E-Rate commitment by declining to sunset or narrow the program The FCC comment opposes conditionally implementing screen-time limits on E-Rate services, emphasizing the importance of maintaining unrestricted access to digital resources for educational purposes.
